n0001.title: The Top of My Todo List
n0001.gist: Reflecting on a nurse's list of dying regrets, the author distills them into a personal anti-cog creed and turns it into daily reminders.
n0001.sourceHeading: The Top of My Todo List

n0002.title: Regrets of the Dying
n0002.gist: A palliative care nurse's list of common deathbed regrets rings true and reveals a pattern of self-diminishment.

n0003.title: Bronnie Ware's List
n0003.gist: Bronnie Ware's list of dying people's regrets seems plausible, and the author admits he could make most of these mistakes himself.

n0004.navLabel: The Top of My Todo List

n0008.navLabel: Bronnie Ware's list of dying people's regrets seems plausible to the author, who could make 4 of 5 mistakes

n0009.title: Portrait of the Cog
n0009.gist: These regrets collectively describe a person who shrinks to fit circumstances and dutifully follows a path until it ends, and such lapses happen by default rather than by choice.

n0010.navLabel: The 5 regrets paint a portrait of post-industrial man who shrinks to fit circumstances and turns dutifully till he stops

n0011.navLabel: The mistakes producing these regrets are errors of omission, dangerous because made by default

n0012.title: Turning Regrets Into Commands
n0012.gist: Since these default mistakes require active reminders to avoid, the author inverts the five regrets into five commands and pins them atop his todo list.

n0013.title: Inverting the Regrets
n0013.gist: Because such omissions occur by default, the author reasons he must be actively reminded to avoid them, so he flips the five regrets into five commands.

n0014.navLabel: Since these mistakes happen by default, the author inverted the 5 regrets into 5 commands to be reminded

n0015.navLabel: Don't ignore your dreams; don't work too much; say what you think; cultivate friendships; be happy

n0016.title: Atop the Todo List
n0016.gist: The author places these five commands at the very top of his todo list as a constant reminder.
